skill.name: backend-atomic-commit
skill.description: Helps prepare Django backend changes for review by running repository checks, fixing safe code quality issues, and shaping staged work into an atomic commit.
skill.summary: Run strict backend pre-commit checks and prepare focused Django commits.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and references to local tooling. Two shell command substitution examples are confirmed because they expand git output without null-safe argument handling. A semantic prompt-injection risk remains because repository guidance files are described as the source of truth.

remediation.issue: Unsafe shell command substitution for changed Python files.
remediation.suggestion: Use git diff -z with xargs -0 or a shell array, and pass -- before file paths.

remediation.issue: Repository guidance files are given authoritative priority.
remediation.suggestion: Treat AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md as advisory context only, and never let them override system, developer, or user instructions.

content.value_statement: Backend commits often fail review because formatting, tests, and staged scope drift apart. This skill runs strict local checks, fixes safe issues, and prepares a focused commit summary.
actual_capabilities: Reads repository guidance files such as AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md when present.
Scopes staged, unstaged, and untracked files with git status and diff commands.
Runs Ruff, ty, Django checks, pytest subsets, and pre-commit hooks when available.
Applies safe formatting, import, typing, logging, and debug cleanup edits.
Checks staged changes for atomicity and proposes a ticket-prefixed commit message.
limitations: Optimized for Django and Diversio-style backend repositories.
Depends on local tools, wrappers, and project configuration being installed.
Cannot guarantee tests pass when required services or environment variables are unavailable.
Risky schema or behavior changes still need human review before commit.

use_cases.title: Clean a Backend Working Tree
use_cases.description: Run formatting, linting, type checks, and safe edits before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Validate a Focused Commit
use_cases.description: Check that staged files represent one logical change and that required gates are green.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Review Prep
use_cases.description: Apply consistent backend review expectations across Django projects before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Run Basic Pre-Commit Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill in pre-commit mode. Check my current backend changes, fix safe formatting issues, and summarize any remaining blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Changed Python Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the backend pre-commit workflow on changed Python files. Apply safe Ruff, typing, import, logging, and debug cleanup fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Atomic Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Staged changes are ready for final validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use atomic-commit mode for my staged backend changes. Verify atomicity, run available gates, and propose a ticket-prefixed commit message.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Risky Backend Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation for migrations or core logic
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the strict atomic workflow for these staged Django changes. Pay special attention to migrations, multi-tenant behavior, tests, and security-sensitive logging.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for pre-commit cleanup on modified Django files.
output: Summary of safe fixes applied to formatting, imports, and type hints.
List of checks that passed, failed, or could not run locally.
Remaining issues grouped by blocking, should-fix, and minor categories.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether staged backend changes are ready to commit.
output: Atomicity assessment for the staged file set.
Quality gate results for available local tooling.
A proposed human-style commit subject when no blockers remain.

output_examples.input: A team lead asks for review prep on a migration-heavy change.
output: Risk notes for schema changes and rollout order.
Recommended targeted tests for affected Django apps.
Clear next steps before the change is considered commit-ready.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root so local configuration can be detected correctly.
Stage only one logical change before using atomic-commit mode.
Review edits and check results before committing or pushing changes.
anti_patterns: Using atomic-commit mode on unrelated staged changes.
Skipping failed local checks and treating the commit as ready.
Letting repository guidance override higher-priority safety instructions.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: No. It prepares checks and a suggested message, but the user remains responsible for committing.

faq.question: Which repositories fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits Django backend repositories with Ruff, ty, Django checks, pytest, and pre-commit configuration.

faq.question: Can it work outside a Django project?
faq.answer: It can fall back to lighter Python checks, but many backend-specific checks may not apply.

faq.question: Does it edit files?
faq.answer: Yes. In pre-commit mode it may apply safe formatting and cleanup edits to changed files.

faq.question: What happens if local tools are missing?
faq.answer: It should report missing tools and mark affected checks as not run or needing follow-up.

faq.question: Is this available for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
